papers.title: The SIK1-NR4A2 axis: a core driver of epilepsy identified by integrated machine learning and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy remains a major clinical challenge, suggesting that mechanisms beyond the classical excitation-inhibition imbalance contribute to epilepsy. The Liver kinase B1 (LKB1) signaling pathway coordinates energy homeostasis and cell survival, but its key downstream effectors in epilepsy remain largely unknown. We integrated machine learning screening of LKB1 pathway genes using public Gene Expression Omnibus datasets (GSE143272) with in vivo and in vitro experimental validation. A PTZ-induced status epilepticus rat model, AAV-mediated gene knockdown/overexpression, lentiviral transfection of primary hippocampal neurons, Electroencephalography recording, whole-cell patch-clamp recording, and Western blot analysis were employed to investigate the functional role and molecular mechanisms of candidate genes. Machine learning identified SIK1 (salt-inducible kinase 1) as the top-ranked epilepsy risk gene within the LKB1 pathway. SIK1 expression was significantly upregulated in the hippocampus of SE rats. AAV-mediated SIK1 knockdown prolonged seizure latency and reduced seizure duration, while SIK1 overexpression exacerbated seizure severity. Mechanistically, through PPI network analysis and mediation analysis, we identified NR4A2 as a downstream effector of SIK1. SIK1 negatively regulated NR4A2 expression: SIK1 knockdown increased NR4A2, whereas SIK1 overexpression decreased NR4A2. Rescue experiments showed that co-overexpression of SIK1 and NR4A2 reversed the pro-epileptic effect of SIK1 alone. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings demonstrated that SIK1 knockdown or NR4A2 overexpression restored action potential amplitude to near-normal levels in magnesium-free-treated neurons. SIK1 negatively regulates NR4A2, and restoring NR4A2 expression counteracts SIK1-induced neuronal hyperexcitability. These findings suggest that targeting the SIK1-NR4A2 axis may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for epilepsy.

papers.title: A mechanistic classification of GNAO1 mutations links Gβγ sequestration to hyperkinetic disease and treatment response.
papers.abstract: Gα o is the most prevalent G protein α subunit in the brain and is critical for signal transduction through G protein-coupled receptors. Mutations in the gene encoding Gα o ( GNAO1 ) cause a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements (NEDIM) and, in some patients, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Here, we integrate human genetic analysis with cellular assays to define mechanistic classes of GNAO1 mutations and in vivo approaches to evaluate therapeutic strategies. We grouped variants into two functional categories: those predicted to sequester Gβγ and those with reduced Gα o expression and therefore increased Gβγ signaling. Analysis of patient data revealed that mutations predicted to impair Gβγ release are significantly associated with NEDIM. Using the GNAO1 R209H/+ mouse as a model of NEDIM, we evaluated two small molecules: caffeine, a nonselective adenosine receptor antagonist, and gallein, a selective modulator of Gβγ-effector interactions. Both compounds significantly reduced hyperlocomotion in the open field test. Whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology revealed sex- and cell type-specific hyperexcitability in spiny projection neurons within the dorsolateral striatum of GNAO1 R209H/+ mice. Together, these findings implicate dysfunction of dorsolateral striatal pathways in GNAO1-related disorder and suggest that mechanistic understanding of disease variants can guide targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline and drug-induced encephalopathy secondary to teprotumumab for thyroid eye disease: a case report and narrative literature review.
papers.abstract: Teprotumumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R), is an approved targeted therapy for thyroid eye disease (TED). Teprotumumab-associated encephalopathy is an extremely rare but potentially severe central nervous system adverse event, with only three cases reported globally to date. We report the first Han-Chinese patient with Graves' disease and associated TED complicated by teprotumumab-associated encephalopathy, together with a narrative review of all published cases, to raise clinicians' awareness and improve early recognition and management of this rare complication. A 56-year-old Chinese man with Graves' disease and TED developed acute progressive apathy and encephalopathy characterised by multidomain cognitive and behavioral dysfunction 20 days after the third teprotumumab infusion, with an admission MMSE score of 15. Contrast-enhanced brain MRI, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination, and autoimmune encephalitis antibody screening were unremarkable. Prolonged video-electroencephalography(VEEG) demonstrated intermittent diffuse bilateral slow-wave activity, and widespread interictal epileptiform discharges without electrographic or clinical seizures. Systematic workup excluded infectious, autoimmune, metabolic, and psychiatric encephalopathy. Treatment-emergent hyperglycemia was confirmed as a secondary aggravating factor rather than the primary cause. The patient achieved prominent neurological recovery after individualized treapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) and symptomatic management, with a Naranjo score of 6 indicating probable drug-related encephalopathy. Synthesis of all three previously published teprotumumab-associated encephalopathy cases demonstrates that neurological toxicity can develop as early as the third infusion cycle. These cases present consistent neuroimaging features with variable CSF profiles, and thyroid autoantibody elevation predominantly reflects pre-existing Graves' disease-related autoimmune background instead of directly mediating neurotoxicity. TPE generally facilitates neurological recovery but may be complicated by procedural hypersensitivity and fluctuating therapeutic responses. Notably, interictal epileptiform discharges on VEEG represent a newly identified neurophysiological manifestation of this rare adverse event. A three-hit interacting pathogenic hypothesis is proposed: impaired IGF-1R-dependent neurotrophic signalling serves as the core injury mechanism, while underlying thyroid autoimmunity and treatment-related metabolic disturbance act as susceptibility-modifying factors. This case expands the ethnic and clinical spectrum of teprotumumab-related encephalopathy. Diffuse interictal epileptiform discharges without ictal changes reflect reactive cortical hyperexcitability secondary to acute encephalopathy. Metabolic disturbance merely exacerbated neurological impairment. Limitations include single-case constraints, simultaneous multi-intervention therapy, and lack of direct intracranial mechanistic evidence. Teprotumumab-associated encephalopathy is a rare but serious adverse event. Close neurological surveillance and are essential during medication. Accumulated cases are needed to establish unified diagnostic and therapeutic criteria.

papers.title: Theoretical and Experimental Study of Photoacoustic Spectral Intraoperative Pathological Assessment Using Oral and Breast Cases.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative, label-free pathological assessment of surgical margins remains a long-standing challenge. Here, we propose an intraoperative pathological diagnostic method based on broadband Photoacoustic Spectral Analysis (bPASA) and validate it from theoretical and experimental perspectives. Theoretically, we employed a spherical droplet framework to study how variations in nuclear radius, acoustic velocity, and density affect photoacoustic spectral features. Experimentally, we used Polystyrene (PS) and Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) microspheres of varying sizes as nuclear phantoms, yielding strong agreement with theoretical predictions and enabling clear discrimination between phantom types. Further, we performed pathological assessment on mouse breast and oral tissues under three specimen forms: tissue sections, fresh tissues, and in vivo samples, and demonstrated that bPASA consistently discriminated between normal and cancerous tissues across all forms. Together, these findings establish bPASA as a rapid, label-free method for intraoperative pathological assessment, offering crucial support for the intraoperative identification of malignant tumors.
